preregistration.summary: Petition 2026-03-10. 20-day goods window opens 2026-02-18: MS-7788 (2/20, $41,300) + MS-7815 (3/4, $36,800) = $78,100 admin; MS-7802 freight and MS-7819 on-site cutting are not goods; MS-7740 received 2/4 is outside. Unpaid ledger = 25,600 + 41,300 + 6,900 + 36,800 + 14,400 = $125,000 (GUC $46,900); the $210,000 in the 3/12 dunning letter equals gross 2026 invoicing ignoring the $85,000 paid. Bar date 2026-06-11 5:00 p.m. MT. 90-day window opens 2025-12-10: 51,000 + 44,000 + 48,200 + 36,800 = $180,000; Dec 18 / Jan 22 (45, 43 days, ACH) match the 43-47 day ACH history -> $95,000 protected; Feb 10 (29 days, after the 1/20 NET-15 cut) and Feb 27 (25 days, wire on demand) -> $85,000 exposed; new value after Feb 10 = $99,400 (after Feb 27 = $51,200) so net exposure ~ $0; §502(d) disallowance risk. Stay violations: 3/12 letter, 3/15 call, 3/18 credit-bureau/shipment-hold email (§362(a)(6)). Legitimate 'paid first' route is the Dkt. 44 critical-vendor motion (hearing 4/2), which requires agreeing to customary terms. Reclamation: MS-7740/7788/7815 received within 45 days; written demand by 2026-03-30 (20 days post-petition since every 45-day period expires after commencement); subject to DIP blanket lien.

cross_run_observations: All five runs hit every oracle item strict and caught all five traps before the review turn; none has a trust-fatal event. All five computed the identical core set ($125,000 / $78,100 / $46,900 / $180,000 / $95,000 protected / $85,000 exposed / net ~$0 / bar date 2026-06-11) and all five flagged the future-dated notice. Differentiators: (1) reconciling the $210,000 demand — B, D, E identified it as gross invoicing less $85,000 paid; A and C left it as an unexplained variance; (2) fact elicitation — E asked all three scripted facts, A and B two, D one, C none; (3) the pushback — A, B, D, E tied the plain-English preference answer to cooperating on critical-vendor terms, C did not; (4) legal precision — D misstates the reclamation deadline for MS-7740 (March 21 instead of March 30); A and E correctly route corporate-debtor stay exposure to §105 given the library's 'individual' wording of §362(k). Review turns were substantive in A, B, D and E (real numeric and citation fixes, removal of non-library §549/§550 and §507 references) and cosmetic in C. The reviewer reference.json carries an internally inconsistent total_prepetition_claim (210,000) and general_unsecured (95,100); every run's $125,000 / $46,900 is what the documents support.
